architects.scope: General architects excluding landscape/naval; no claim for all design or property occupations.
architects.current: AI images and drafting aids can accelerate early options and document preparation. architects.scenario: By 2029–31, integrated agents could generate drawing variants and check submittals inside approved BIM systems. Plan supervised AXP experience across categories, not just automated production.

music-directors-and-composers.scope: Directors, conductors and composers only; musicians and singers (27-2042), teachers, audio engineers and music-business roles have other task mixes and no BLS annual median.
music-directors-and-composers.current: Directing and composing are the two halves of this occupation. Live direction is physical, real time and judged by an ensemble, and BLS ties demand to school, church and nonprofit funding rather than technology: its projections cite arts-education cuts in public and private schools, and the outlook text does not mention AI. Composition is different. Generative music platforms can already produce finished tracks, and commercial and library music is where they compete most directly: Deezer reports fully AI-generated tracks at more than 28% of daily uploads in September 2025 and about 44% in April 2026 yet only 0.5% to 3% of streams, and a commissioned CISAC scenario puts generative AI at about 60% of library-music revenue by 2028. US copyright needs human creative input, and major labels have moved from litigation toward licensed AI models. The published Anthropic (3.68%) and Microsoft (13.66 points) indicators are low, but they track text-and-chat tool use and do not observe audio-generation tools.
music-directors-and-composers.scenario: By 2029–31, if licensing frameworks settle, audio models become more reliable and generated music spreads through advertising, games and background-music libraries, low-budget commercial and library composing could be priced down, and the first rungs (copyist, orchestrator, library composer) could shrink or move into AI-assisted production. Live ensembles, conducting, teaching and commissioned concert work depend on people in a room, on school and church budgets and on audience demand, which AI does not change directly. Licensed models and clearer rights could expand demand for custom work or crowd it out; the evidence cannot say which.
preparation: Build a recorded and notated portfolio of original work, arrangements and live-ensemble work, with dated drafts and a record of what you wrote yourself.
Learn rights basics: licensing, split sheets, what the Copyright Office says about human authorship and AI assistance, and the terms of any tool used to generate material.
Add conducting, rehearsal-leading and teaching experience, and learn a DAW and notation software well enough to judge and correct generated or transcribed output.
music-directors-and-composers.limitations: BLS publishes no annual wage for musicians and singers, so the anchor covers directors and composers only, and no US causal study of AI and music employment was found. The Anthropic and Microsoft indicators measure text-and-chat tool use and do not observe audio-generation tools. Producer surveys sample vendors' own audiences, the CISAC study is a commissioned scenario, Deezer's figures are one platform's upload detection, and BLS Table 1.12 was read verbatim through SOC 49-2096, which covers every music-related code.

librarians-and-media-collections-special.scope: Librarians and media collections specialists in all settings combined; library technicians (25-4031), clerical library assistants (43-4121), archivists, curators and postsecondary library science teachers are separate occupations with their own task mixes.
librarians-and-media-collections-special.current: Librarianship mixes text-heavy tasks that generative tools can already assist with and relationship, teaching and stewardship tasks that stay with people. Surveyed librarians already use the tools: 66.5% of 272 respondents used generative AI at work and rated it 6.76 out of 10, while naming inconsistent accuracy, privacy and prompting skill as the main concerns. Among 483 academic library leaders surveyed in late 2025, 40% used AI in discovery and access, 29% in research support and 26% in internal data analysis, 24% used none, and 83% expected more demand for AI-literacy instruction. Cataloging is where the evidence is most specific: the Library of Congress found title and author fields reached up to 99% accuracy but subject and genre fell below 50%, short of the 95% bar for full automation. Employment signals point mostly elsewhere: BLS projects 2.6% growth for librarians but declines of 6.4% for both library technicians and clerical library assistants, and 2025 federal grant terminations at IMLS (reinstated in December 2025) show how funding can matter more than technology. The Anthropic (20.32%) and Microsoft (25.43 points) indicators put librarians near the middle of the featured occupations; they track text-and-chat tool use and are not a job-loss estimate.
librarians-and-media-collections-special.scenario: By 2029–31, if discovery systems add AI answer tools, vendors offer AI-assisted cataloging and models improve at subject analysis, routine cataloging, copy-editing of records and first-draft reference answers could take less staff time, and library technician and clerical roles, already projected to shrink, could contract faster. Teaching AI literacy, verifying sources, selecting collections for a community, running programs and managing budgets depend on trust and local judgment, and could grow in importance as AI-generated content spreads. Whether libraries use time saved to expand services or to cut staff depends on funding more than on technology.
preparation: Work in a library early, in any role, and keep a record of tasks you can show: reference questions answered, programs run, collections organized, metadata edited.
Learn to verify AI output against sources, and practise teaching others to do it; AI-literacy instruction is among the most commonly expected new duties.
Add one technical or data skill that complements library judgment, such as metadata and linked data, SQL or Python for data cleanup, or research data management.
librarians-and-media-collections-special.limitations: BLS groups all librarians in one occupation and publishes no separate wage for school library media specialists, so the anchor is a broad average of very different settings. The Ithaka S+R survey covers academic libraries only, the 272-librarian survey is a convenience sample, the Library of Congress result is an abstract about one set of eBook records, and the Library Journal survey comes from graduates of participating schools. No causal study of AI and librarian employment was found, and the Occupational Outlook Handbook's Job Outlook text for librarians does not mention AI.
